steps.content: [Lighthouse Top at Sunrise]
Scorched awake by the piercing sun, you struggle to open leaden eyelids. The world slowly resolves from a blur of glare into a warm, bright clarity, illuminating every corner of the desolate island.
Ceto sits quietly beside you, seemingly awake for some time. Both your wounds have been neatly dressed—undoubtedly with high-grade medical supplies you'd never find around the lighthouse.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Finally awake? The sun's practically baking your back.
Her tone is as rigid as ever, but you don't miss the faint, unguarded amusement at the corner of her lips.

You attempt to sit up, but barely an inch off the ground, every muscle in your body stages a mutiny. A delayed, crushing wave of pain washes over you. With a dull thud, you collapse back down, surrendering completely to the earth, splayed out like a starfish.

Sunlight cascades without restraint, warming your skin to the point of heat. The sensation is almost decadent. Gone is the chill of the Black Tide, the putrid sea breeze; all that remains is this pure, nearly scorching light. The perpetual shroud over this island has finally broken.

In the distance, the shoreline teems with methodical activity. The Rancor troops move with disciplined efficiency, scouring the last traces of contamination. The commander's voice, sharp and clear, crackles through a loudspeaker, signaling the operation's end.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: You won. DisCity came for OT-N07.
We both made it out alive. Our bet...
You stop mid-sentence. The recipe from Miles, the very prize of your bet, is now pointless. Its main ingredient, Tide Crawler, is being systematically erased from the world.

The bloodshed and chill of the long night have vanished, evaporated by the sun. You lie side-by-side, a wordless exhaustion intertwining with an equally profound gratitude, flowing silently between you.

This silence isn't empty, but full. It holds the taste of sunshine on each breath and the strong, steady beat of hearts beneath your ribs—a relentless reminder that you are alive, truly alive. The serenity of survival resonates more powerfully than any celebration could.
Next, I'm going to have some proper rest. A grand feast! And I'm sleeping for three days straight!
You start counting on your fingers:
First, a bowl of stew so hot it steams up the room, then honey wine so sweet it'll make your teeth hurt, and finally, a real, actual bed...

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: I thought you had someone waiting for you. Important things to do.
You raise your hand, gazing at the power of the shackles in your palm—now faded to a dying ember, nearly gone.
Exactly. That's why I need to be at my best.
I have to be in top form... for when I go to bring her home.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Home...
Her gaze drifts toward the skyline where DisCity rises, a land she has never set foot on, yet has carried on her shoulders for half a lifetime. It was her comrades' homeland. But where is her own?
What about you? The Black Tide is cleared. The lighthouse doesn't need to signal anymore. What's next?

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: I think I'll look around.
Huh?

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: I want to see what their loyalty and sacrifice actually bought, with my own eyes. Find a few places I actually want to go. Now that I'm free of this place... I want to see what's out there.
She holds the gleaming tags up to the sunlight, where the inscribed names seem to jostle and play, jockeying for the light.
[Shore]

The receded tide has laid bare a desolate seabed. Across the dried silt, the wreckage of the battlefield emerges: monster carcasses, scattered bleached bones, broken firearms, blades eaten by rust, and metal limbs so mangled their original forms are beyond recognition.
The Rancor ships have raised their flag, signaling their readiness to depart.
Are you sure you won't come with us? That uniform will make you a target out there.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: No. I was just an orphan the keepers took in. Just a lighthouse keeper. Nothing more.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: I'm not chasing the power in this blade. I'm looking for a new lighthouse.
She looks toward the bow of the ship, and you follow her gaze. Catherine is standing there, waving to you, waiting for you to rejoin the team.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Do you trust her? That she can really help bring your friend back?

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Fair enough. There are no prophets on the battlefield. Good luck, then.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: We'll meet again, Chief of the Minos Bureau of Crisis Control. I made a deal with your general.
A deal?

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: If you want to know, come help me.
She ignores your question and walks straight onto the mudflats, pushing aside the damp sand to retrieve a long blade, rusted and dulled beyond any sharpness.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Take these Rancors left on the battlefield. Bring them where they're needed most.
The morning sunlight falls obliquely across your bodies, illuminating your repeated motions—bending down, picking up, wiping the mud from each weapon.

You do not press her for what passed between her and Augustus.
Behind you, the weather-beaten lighthouse stands its silent watch. Ahead lies an old battlefield, and a new journey.
[DisCorps Conference Room]

5 days 5 hours 7 minutes

steps.speaker: Scarface
steps.content: Wait, what? They were already messing with Aurum Secretum back then?!

steps.speaker: Military Doctor
steps.content: The sorcery patterns are similar, but this is clearly a failed prototype. The samples we retrieved only prove someone tried to merge contamination with a nuclear warhead a long time ago—a two-pronged approach.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Perhaps we can consider a bolder theory. The nuke was just a pretext. Their real objective was the Mania contamination all along.

steps.speaker: Military Doctor
steps.content: Talk about malicious intent. So, what do we do with these Rancors? Do we keep them?

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Of course. We can never have too much gear.
The Black Tide was also Adelaide's doing? That bastard...

A slender form detaches itself from the shadows, and the room hushes, as if a taut string had been plucked. The newcomer's physical injuries have healed, but the person within has grown more fractured. While all others avert their gaze, Augustus alone remains a steady gravitational force, faced with the primed explosive.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Not necessarily. But if you need a target for your frustration, be my guest.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: If a failed Aurum Secretum experiment can cause a mess like the Black Tide, then this little excursion is about to get serious. So, what do you say? Still up for it, little Chief?

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Or should I get used to calling you "Commander"?
[Chief's Military Uniform Portrait]
In a cemetery outside DisCity, a new stone monument stands quietly. Its strikingly traditional design sets it in silent dissonance against the modern markers that surround it.

This monument was originally intended for the city's memorial park, but the request was denied. The applicant had wished for these names to rest far from the echoes of war, believing they belonged among the ordinary citizens they once were.

The stone has been meticulously cleaned, revealing rows of freshly engraved names. Before it, an array of offerings is spread out: hamburgers, fried chicken, the latest fashion magazines, game cartridges, cosmetics, cigarettes, and alcohol...
Only when not an inch of space remains does the visitor finally cease, leaving the memorial laden with the tokens of a life lived.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: It'll be a while before I can visit again. So don't you bastards go talking shit about me.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: I think I found a new lighthouse. I'm going to see if they've got a place for someone like me.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: You know I don't have much to offer. Guarding a lighthouse. Fighting... That's about it.
Words linger on her lips, but time denies them. She rises solemnly, her gaze fixed on the names etched in stone, paying a moment of silent respect.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: I told you we'd meet again.
At her waist, the badge of her new squad, Broken Blade, catches the light.
Success is not final. Failure is not fatal. It is the courage to continue that counts.
